dataset.benign_source: Tranco top-1m.csv.zip (top 100k domains, full URLs synthesised with realistic paths) + 240 synthetic benign shortener URLs (de-biasing step) + 1,500 benign URLs on mainstream new gTLDs (.online/.site/.shop/.tech/...) from Tranco ranks 100k-1M (Nov 9 de-biasing: the top-100k set almost never shows a legitimate new-gTLD site, which taught the model that those endings mean phishing)

augmentation.applied_to: training split only (never validation or test)
augmentation.method: Seeded synthetic phishing URLs (scripts/augment.py) teaching the model the deep tricks that are rare in the real feeds: homoglyph/ASCII/near-miss brand mutations, '@'-trick decoys, file-extension TLDs, open-redirect laundering, invisible Unicode characters, and login pages on free hosting.

splits.grouped_by: registered domain (no domain leaks across splits)

rule_detector.note: Rule score alone, mapped with the tuned thresholds.

combined.note: Headline score = 0.5 * rule score + 0.5 * model probability * 100. '3-level accuracy' counts a Medium verdict as wrong because the test truth has only High (phishing) and Low (benign); the High false-alarm rate and recall describe the headline verdict fairly.

limitations: Benign URLs are synthesised from Tranco domain names, so their paths are simpler than real browsing; the model may partly key on URL length. The rule-based detector needs no training data and is reported alongside as a cross-check.
URL-only analysis cannot catch phishing hosted on legitimate or compromised domains.
PhishTank skews toward freshly reported, short-lived phishing pages; performance on older or targeted attacks may differ.
